title: Resilience & Fallback Sales Deck for Critical Inference
author: Nadia Kline
body:
Overview
========

Purpose: This document is a field-ready sales deck and evidence pack that surfaces Redwood Inference's resilience and graceful-degradation story for mission-critical inference workloads (finance fraud detection, live customer support routing, automated decisioning). It bundles positioning, competitive differentiators, a slide-level pitch outline, pilot pricing guidance, a short case study, technical rollout patterns, and a security FAQ for buyer conversations.

Use: Sales engineers and account teams should use this as a single-page narrative + slide checklist when proposing pilots to prospects that require high availability, predictable latency, and clear fallback guarantees.

Key message (one-liner)
-----------------------
"Predictable inference when everything else fails: keep latency SLOs, control unit economics, and preserve confidentiality with tiered fallbacks and multi-path routing."

Positioning & Messaging (3 elevator lines)
----------------------------------------
- For platform and infra teams that must guarantee uninterrupted user experiences, Redwood provides an inference runtime and control plane that prioritizes reliability and graceful degradation over ideal-case throughput numbers.
- Unlike single-endpoint cloud APIs or self-built runtimes, Redwood couples an operational playbook (canaries, automatic fallback policies, cross-region routing) with economic controls so resilience is measurable and affordable.
- Our default selling point: SLAs you can instrument (uptime, latency SLOs, error budgets) and automated fallbacks that prevent application-visible failures.

Competitive Brief (quick takeaways)
----------------------------------
Competitors considered: public cloud model endpoints, large API-first LLM providers, and self-managed inference stacks.

Differentiators (table as text)
- Smart routing and fallbacks: route to cheaper/compatible model variants or regionally isolated Dedicated pools when primary capacity is constrained.
- Observability-first: token-level cost & latency breakdowns, route tracing, and automatic regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
- Operational guarantees: canary rollouts, A/B controlled rollouts, transparent rollback triggers based on quality and latency thresholds.
- Cost controls: batching and caching recommendations specific to workload, quantization profiles, and precise per-route unit economics.

Performance & SLO snapshots (typical published benchmarks)
- Hosted API (general workloads): p50 35–60ms, p95 110–220ms depending on model size and sequence length.
- Dedicated reserved pools: p50 20–40ms, p95 70–150ms for optimized-medium models.
- Platform SLA examples: 99.95% uptime, target p95 latency for a given route with error budget tied to token-level retries.

Pitch Deck Outline (12-slide recommended flow)
------------------------------------------------
1) Cover: Logo, prospect name, meeting date, objective (pilot ask).
2) Problem: What breaks in production (latency spikes, model-serving outages, cost overruns, regulatory constraints).
3) Why it matters: user/business impact with KPI examples (abandon rate, fraud loss, revenue per minute).
4) Redwood value prop: unified runtime + fallbacks + observability.
5) How it works (simplified diagram): request routing -> KV/prefix cache -> model variants -> fallback paths.
6) Resilience model: SLOs, retry/circuit-breaker logic, fallback tiers (same-model-smaller, distilled variant, cached response).
7) Security & compliance: VPC/private, KMS/HSM, audit logs.
8) Pricing & pilot structure: example pricing scenarios (see below).
9) Case study: short wins from a comparable customer (results and metrics).
10) Pilot plan & success criteria: timelines, data access, monitoring checklist.
11) Next steps & commercial ask: pilot length, committed throughput or burst credits.
12) Appendix & technical contact: integration owner and SRE contact.

Pilot Pricing Guidance (field-ready scripts and examples)
-------------------------------------------------------
Guiding principle: For resilience pilots, price for predictability, not just tokens. Structure pilots to allow capacity guarantees and observable metrics.

Sample pilot models (numbers are example guidance for field conversations):
- Trial (proof-of-concept): 2–4 week window, $0 setup, free credits up to $5k for hosted API with monitoring instrumentation.
- Resilience Pilot (recommended): 6–8 weeks, dedicated small pool (N GPU equivalents), $12k/month (discounted trial price), includes SRE onboarding, route-level dashboards, and automated fallback policy set-up.
- Proof to Commit: Convert pilot metrics to a committed Dedicated offering: e.g., 2x pilot throughput committed for 12 months at $45k/month with priority support and a 99.95% SLA.

Example per-token framing for conversations: use token-equivalent units (TEUs) for cross-model comparisons.
- Hosted baseline: $0.0007 per generation token for medium models (ballpark; aim for customer-specific quoting).
- Dedicated amortized: effectively $0.0003–$0.0005 per token once reserved throughput and batching optimizations are applied for steady workloads.

Commercial ask scripts (example wording)
- "To validate resilience end-to-end we recommend a six-week Resilience Pilot: we’ll provision a small Dedicated pool, instrument three critical routes, and implement two fallback tiers. If your systems meet the success criteria (p95 latency under X ms, <0.5% fallbacks to cached responses), we’ll translate telemetry into a reserved-capacity proposal you can evaluate."

Field Playbook: Objections & Responses (common prospect concerns)
---------------------------------------------------------------
- Objection: "We cannot tolerate any data leakage to third parties."
  Response: "We offer Private deployment with customer-managed VPC and optional on-prem packaging; keys remain in your KMS/HSM and audit logs are exported to your SIEM."
- Objection: "What happens if primary model capacity is exhausted?"
  Response: "We’ll configure multi-tier fallbacks: 1) reroute to your Dedicated pool, 2) fall back to a lightweight compatible model we host with lower cost, 3) serve cached or templated responses with graceful downgrade messaging to users. All fallbacks are counted in metrics and visible in the dashboard."
- Objection: "How do you guarantee the fallback quality?"
  Response: "Fallback models are pre-evaluated on your prompt set and have automatic quality gates; we only enable fallback paths that meet a defined BLEU/accuracy threshold or pass your custom eval harness."

Technical Appendix: Integration & Rollout Patterns
--------------------------------------------------
Minimum required items for a resilience pilot:
- Test prompt corpus (1k–10k examples) covering edge cases and typical length distributions.
- Defined success metrics: p95 latency target, fallback rate ceiling, false positive/negative thresholds for quality.
- Network connectivity: whitelist Redwood control-plane IPs for Dedicated/VPC onboarding, or provide peering details for Private.

Canary / Rollout recipe (recommended)
1) Provision route in staging with tracing enabled.
2) Run synthetic traffic for 48–72 hours, collect p50/p95/p99 and error counts.
3) Enable canary (2–5% of production traffic) with automatic rollback if daily error rate exceeds 0.2% or p95 increases by >40%.
4) Gradually increase to 25%, monitor for 72 hours, then switch traffic.

Sample API snippet (fallback policy)
```json
{ "route": "/messages/generate", "slo": { "p95_ms": 150 }, "fallback_policy": [
  { "type": "same-model-quantized", "max_latency_ms": 200 },
  { "type": "smaller-variant", "model": "redwood-compact-3b", "max_latency_ms": 300 },
  { "type": "kv_cache_response", "max_age_seconds": 3600 }
] }
```
(Use this example in technical appendix slides to show that fallback policies are declarative and instrumented.)

Case Study: ParcelPro (logistics) — two-page customer brief
---------------------------------------------------------
Context: ParcelPro is a large logistics platform that runs real-time address normalization and delivery exception triage. Their user-facing systems historically suffered from model-serving outages during Black Friday-like peaks.

Challenge:
- Spiky inference demand during peak windows increased p95 latency to >700ms and caused ~4% request failures that translated to delayed deliveries and customer support overload.

Redwood solution:
- Provisioned a Dedicated pool for critical routes, configured automatic multi-tier fallback (quantized variant + cached responses), and implemented prefix-KV caching for repetitive address normalizations.

Outcome (measured in pilot):
- p95 latency reduced from 700ms to 120ms for critical route.
- Failures visible to applications dropped from 4% to 0.03% (exceeded 99.95% uptime target).
- Unit cost for peak windows dropped 31% due to batching and quantization profiles.

Buyer quote (paraphrased): "Redwood allowed us to stop apologizing for downtime — our routing system stayed resilient through the busiest weekend we’ve seen."

Security & Compliance FAQ (top questions for prospect meetings)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: Data residency is configured per-customer. For Hosted we provide region controls and retention policies configurable by route (default 90 days for logs, 30 days for KV cache metadata). Private deployments mirror customer policies.

Q: Can I bring my own KMS/HSM?
A: Yes. We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and customer HSM integrations for key wrapping and signing of model artifacts.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and SIEM integration?
A: Yes — all request/response metadata, authorization events, and fallback activations are exported via our audit pipeline to S3/BigQuery/your SIEM with configurable retention.

Q: What certifications or independent audits do you have?
A: We maintain SOC 2 Type II and perform annual penetration testing with third-party vendors; we supply audit artifacts under NDA for enterprise due diligence.

Q: How are fallbacks tested for model safety and data leakage?
A: Fallback variants are vetted in the same onboarding eval harness as primary models. We run tokenizer-based leakage scans and prompt-perturbation tests before enabling fallback.

Next steps (playbook for closing a resilience pilot)
1) Discovery call: 60-minute technical and business alignment; capture SLOs and critical routes.
2) Proposal: 3–5 business days to produce pilot scope, monitoring checklist, and provisional quote.
3) Onboarding: 1–2 week setup with platform + SRE pairing.
4) Pilot run: 6–8 weeks with weekly syncs and a final telemetry review.
5) Commercial conversion: translate pilot telemetry into committed capacity and SLA contract.
